resources.string: Your notes live in a folder
Point Pocket Prose at the folder your writing is already in. Nothing is copied or moved — your notes stay exactly where they are.
That folder isn\'t there any more
Pocket Prose can\'t reach the folder you chose. It may have been moved, renamed, or removed with an SD card. Your notes are not affected.
No notes in this folder yet
This note is open for reading only
Pocket Prose can\'t be certain it would save this note exactly as it found it, so it won\'t change it at all. You can still read it here, and edit it anywhere else.
The note keeps its title. Only its name in the folder changes.
Your folder cannot hold every character. It would be called “%1$s”.
Your folder cannot hold every character, so this leaves the name it already has.
Another note already has that name.
No lines to leave out. Start a line with + to keep it out of the draft, like +an alternative.
The note is removed from your folder. Pocket Prose cannot bring it back.
The note could not be deleted
A tag can\'t have a space in it — try a hyphen, like meta-info.
A tag can\'t have a # in it.
While you were writing, this note was edited on another device. Pocket Prose has not touched either version.
Nothing on this phone can open that file
No tags on these notes yet.

As far as I\'m concerned, I am a writer — whether my writing\'s spoken or written in a blog, paper, book or printed on the side of a submarine.
How your notes are set on screen. Your phone\'s own text size still applies on top of this.
The library opens showing only this tag. If the tag is missing when the app starts, it opens showing everything.
Notes carrying this tag sit at the top of the library. It is an ordinary tag in every other way: it appears in the drawer while a note carries it, and renaming it there renames it here.

resources.string: Write tags and titles into the text
For editors that read them there. Your folder stays as it is.
I built Pocket Prose for my own lyrics, which live in a folder and are going to stay there. Maybe your writing does too.

This app doesn\'t track. Anything.\nThe downside is I have no idea if or how often it\'s used or downloaded.\nCould be zero, could be a secret cult following. I genuinely don\'t know.
Am I wasting my time publishing it? You tell me.
There are three (maybe more) ways to keep me motivated:
Opens a page on my website with a like button. Nothing is counted until you press it — just the press and an anonymised IP.
A star is a number I can actually see, and it helps others find it.
Entirely optional. The app is and stays free either way.
